knowledge_rule: Stage 1 risk flag when the customer's 'closeBoundary' answer is anything other than exactly 'No'
provenance_status: historical individual provenance not yet identified

source_baseline.contains: the trigger (closeBoundary !== 'No'), the exact customer-facing text, the category ('programme') and the discipline ('planning') exactly as migrated. Same source baseline commit as Migration Slices 3/4.

question_wording_provenance_note: The Stage 1 'closeBoundary' question wording and position were reworded 27 August 2026 (Stage 1 Map Control Layout + 17-Question Workflow task, application commit 998ef610b3bbc91071cbeac2651c919520a08119) — this did NOT change the fact key, the three answer values, this rule's trigger, its text, its category or its discipline.
discipline_label_note: discipline='planning' is a presentation-only grouping tag (see runStage1Risks()'s own governing comment: 'planning' = boundary/neighbour/approvals-adjacent). It is NOT a dependency on, or reference to, the separate, heavily-governed Planning Intelligence subsystem (evidence.js Planning Batches 1-5, LOCKED/PROTECTED per DECISION-LOG.md). This rule reads only p.facts.closeBoundary, a plain Stage 1 Yes/No/Not-sure answer, with zero code-level or data-level connection to Planning Intelligence. The shared word is a naming coincidence, not an architectural dependency.
inequality_behaviour_note: closeBoundary !== 'No' is an inequality against a single literal, not an allowlist. 'Yes', 'Not sure', empty string, null, undefined and any unrecognised value all trigger the risk — deliberately preserved.
